sections.label: Singapore 2019 economic growth
sections.summary: Singapore's economy grew by a modest 0.7% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singapore's economy grew by a modest 0.7% in 2019.

sections.label: MTI downgrades GDP forecast
sections.summary: The Ministry of Trade and Industry downgraded the GDP forecast from between 0.5% and 2.5% to between -0.5% and 1.5%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) has downgraded the gross domestic product (GDP) forecast from between 0.5% and 2.5%, to between -0.5% and 1.5%.

sections.label: Additional $800 million for outbreak
sections.summary: Frontline agencies have been fighting and containing the outbreak, and an additional $800 million is set aside in this Budget to support these efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our frontline agencies have been fighting and containing the outbreak.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside an additional $800 million in this Budget to support these efforts.

sections.label: Two special packages, $5.6 billion
sections.summary: With uncertainties and concern about impact on businesses and jobs, two special packages with a total budget of $5.6 billion will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With these uncertainties, I know Singaporeans are understandably very concerned about the impact on our businesses and jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will introduce two special packages, with a total budget of $5.6 billion.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package
sections.summary: As Ng Chee Meng and union leaders said every worker matters, a Stabilisation and Support Package amounting to $4 billion will be provided.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As the National Trades Union Congress Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng and his union leaders said, "Every worker matters".

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will, therefore, provide a Stabilisation and Support Package, amounting to $4 billion.

sections.label: Offsetting 8% of wages
sections.summary: For every local worker in employment, 8% of wages will be offset, up to a monthly wage cap of $3,600, for three months.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For every local worker in employment, I will offset 8% of the wages, up to a monthly wage cap of $3,600, for three months.

sections.label: Working Capital Loan enhancement
sections.summary: The Enterprise Financing Scheme's Working Capital Loan component is enhanced for one year, raising the maximum loan quantum from $300,000 to $600,000 and increasing risk-share to 80%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To help enterprises access working capital more easily, I will also enhance the Enterprise Financing Scheme's Working Capital Loan component for one year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will raise the maximum loan quantum from $300,000 to $600,000, and increase our risk-share on these loans to 80%, from the current 50% to 70%.

sections.label: Sectors affected by COVID-19
sections.summary: Five sectors directly affected by COVID-19 will get additional support: tourism, aviation, retail, food services and point-to-point transport services.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Sectors directly affected by COVID-19 will get additional support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These five sectors are: tourism, aviation, retail, food services and point-to-point transport services.

sections.label: Supporting local workers
sections.summary: Together with the Jobs Support Scheme, employers in these sectors will be supported to retain and train more than 330,000 local workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Together with the Jobs Support Scheme, we will support employers in these sectors to retain and train more than 330,000 local workers.

sections.label: Tourism Temporary Bridging Loan
sections.summary: For tourism enterprises, a Temporary Bridging Loan Programme will be introduced for a year with Participating Financial Institutions, with loan quantum up to $1 million and interest capped at 5%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For enterprises in the tourism sector, we will be working with Participating Financial Institutions to introduce a Temporary Bridging Loan Programme for a year, with a loan quantum of up to $1 million and interest rate capped at 5%.

sections.label: GST increase not in 2021
sections.summary: After reviewing revenue and expenditure projections and the economy, the GST rate increase will not take effect in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: After reviewing our revenue and expenditure projections and considering the current state of the economy, I have decided that the GST rate increase will not take effect in 2021.

sections.label: GST increase needed by 2025
sections.summary: Recurrent revenue sources are still required for medium-term recurrent spending, so the GST increase will still be needed by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And we will still require recurrent sources of revenue to fund our recurrent spending needs in the medium term.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Thus, the GST increase will still be needed by 2025.

sections.label: GST Assurance Package offsets
sections.summary: A $6 billion Assurance Package will cushion the GST increase, giving most Singaporean households offsets covering at least five years of additional GST expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And just as we have done in the past, we will provide an Assurance Package when the GST rate is raised.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will be a $6 billion package for Singaporeans, to cushion the increase as we transition to the higher GST rate.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The majority of Singaporean households will receive offsets to cover at least five years’ worth of additional GST expenses incurred.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, the majority of Singaporean households will receive offsets to cover at least five years' worth of additional GST expenses incurred.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Those living in 1- to 3‑room HDB flats will receive offsets equivalent to about 10 years’ worth of additional GST expenses incurred.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Under the Assurance Package for GST, every adult Singaporean will receive a cash payout of $700 to $1,600 over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To illustrate, a family of four with a combined income of $6,000 living in a 4‑room HDB flat can receive about $7,000 in offsets over five years in total.

sections.label: Assurance Package GSTV Fund
sections.summary: The speaker will set aside $6 billion for the Assurance Package in the GSTV Fund in this year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To meet this commitment, I will set aside $6 billion for the Assurance Package in the GSTV Fund in this year’s Budget.

sections.label: Future Economy Council and ITMs
sections.summary: The Future Economy Council was set up in 2017 with 23 Industry Transformation Maps, and productivity rose 2.6% per year over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We recognised these changes early and made an early start on economic transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We set up the Future Economy Council (FEC) in 2017 and we now have 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the last three years, overall productivity, as measured by real value‑added per actual hour worked, rose by 2.6% per year.

sections.label: Real median income growth
sections.summary: Between 2016 and 2019, real median income for Singaporeans grew by 3.7% per year, up from 3.2% per year previously.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2019, real median income for Singaporeans grew by 3.7% per year, up from 3.2% per year in the preceding three years.

sections.label: Transformation and Growth allocation
sections.summary: Including sums allocated in previous years, a total of $8.3 billion is being allocated over the next three years to Transformation and Growth.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Including sums allocated in previous years, I am allocating a total of $8.3 billion over the next three years to enable Transformation and Growth.

sections.label: Digital Economy Agreement concluded
sections.summary: Last month, Singapore concluded its first Digital Economy Agreement with Chile and New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Just last month, we concluded our first Digital Economy Agreement with Chile and New Zealand.

sections.label: FinTech investment growth
sections.summary: Annual FinTech investments rose six-fold between 2015 and 2019 to over $1 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2019, annual investments in financial technology (FinTech) have risen six-fold to over $1 billion.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore support programmes
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will launch an Executive-in-Residence pilot for over 10 TACs and a Heartland Enterprise Upgrading Programme for merchants' associations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will launch a pilot Executive‑in‑Residence programme to fund more than 10 TACs covering all sectors of the economy to hire experienced executives and provide expert advice to enterprises in their industries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Likewise, merchants’ associations play a critical role in upgrading heartland enterprises, such as what the Chong Pang City Merchant and Hawker's Association has done.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, Enterprise Singapore will launch a new Heartland Enterprise Upgrading Programme to support merchants' associations to drive transformation of heartland enterprises.

sections.label: Startup SG Equity deep-tech funding
sections.summary: An additional $300 million under Startup SG Equity is expected to draw over $800 million in private funding over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To catalyse investment into deep-tech startups, I will set aside an additional $300 million under the Startup SG Equity.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We expect this to draw in more than $800 million of private funding over the next 10 years.

sections.label: Enterprise Grow Package enhancement
sections.summary: Support through schemes like SMEs Go Digital and Market Readiness Assistance will be enhanced this year via an Enterprise Grow Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have been supporting them through schemes, such as the SMEs Go Digital programme and the Market Readiness Assistance grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, we will enhance support for these enterprises through an Enterprise Grow Package.

sections.label: EDG project support increase
sections.summary: In FY2020, about 3,000 projects are expected to be supported through EDG, over 10% more than today.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In FY2020, we expect to support about 3,000 projects through EDG, an increase of more than 10% from the number today.

sections.label: 70-70 overseas exposure target
sections.summary: A "70-70" target and new Asia-Ready Exposure Programme aim to give local IHL graduates overseas experience, with enhanced Global Ready Talent internships.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support our local students to acquire cross-cultural skills and understand our region better, we will set ourselves a "70-70" target – 70% of local IHL graduates to have an overseas experience, and 70% of this group to have exposure to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), China or India.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To achieve this target, we will introduce a new Asia-Ready Exposure Programme to support local youths' visits to cities in ASEAN, China or India.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will also enhance support for internships under the Global Ready Talent Programme.

sections.label: Training participation and SkillsFuture Credit
sections.summary: Training participation rose from 35% in 2015 to 49% in 2019, and SkillsFuture Credit helped over half a million Singaporeans by end 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The training participation rate has risen from 35% in 2015 to 49% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As of end 2019, the SkillsFuture Credit has helped more than half a million Singaporeans pick up new skills and develop new interests.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up
sections.summary: A one-off $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up will be provided for every Singaporean aged 25 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, to support Singaporeans to continue learning, I will provide a one-off SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500 for every Singaporean aged 25 and above.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit and related measures
sections.summary: A $10,000 per enterprise SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit will benefit over 35,000 enterprises, mostly SMEs, alongside expanded Productivity Solutions Grant and Work-Study Programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, I will introduce a new SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit to encourage employers to embark on the transformation of their workforce and enterprise in tandem.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit, at $10,000 per enterprise, will benefit over 35,000 enterprises, most of which will be SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Productivity Solutions Grant supports enterprises to adopt pre-approved digital solutions and equipment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will expand the Productivity Solutions Grant to include job redesign consultancy services.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By helping to raise the skills of workers in these SMEs, the entire supply chain benefits.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We aim to partner up to 40 of such anchor enterprises to benefit 4,000 SMEs over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Fourth, our IHLs will work with more enterprises to enable local students to learn in a real work setting, through SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will now more than double the capacity of these programmes by 2025.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package
sections.summary: A new SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package will help locals in their 40s and 50s stay employable and move to new jobs or roles.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will do more to support them.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will introduce a new SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package for locals in their 40s and 50s to help them stay employable and move on to new jobs or new roles.

sections.label: Senior Worker Support Package measures
sections.summary: A Senior Worker Support Package comprises a Senior Employment Credit, CPF Transition Offset, Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and Part-Time Re-employment Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To ease in these changes for employers and workers, I will introduce a Senior Worker Support Package comprising four measures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, I will refashion SEC and ASEC into a Senior Employment Credit, which will take effect from 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, when employer CPF contribution rates go up in 2021, we will provide employers with a CPF Transition Offset for the year, to offset half of the increase in employer contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Third, we will introduce the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant to support enterprises that raise their own Retirement and Re-employment ages ahead of the legislated changes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Fourth, we will introduce the Part-Time Re‑employment Grant to support and encourage enterprises to formalise part-time re-employment provisions.

sections.label: S Pass sub-DRC reductions
sections.summary: The S Pass sub-DRCs of the Construction, Marine Shipyard and Process sectors will be reduced from 20% to 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Therefore, this year, we will take further steps.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will reduce the S Pass sub‑DRCs of the Construction, Marine Shipyard and Process sectors from 20% to 15%.

sections.label: Healthcare, education, housing expenditure increases
sections.summary: Between 2010 and 2019 healthcare, education and national development spending rose, with most national development funds going to public housing subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Between 2010 and 2019, we tripled our healthcare expenditure from $4 billion to about $12 billion a year, to meet the growing needs of our seniors and to ensure that every Singaporean has access to affordable and quality healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We increased our investments in education, from $10 billion to about $13 billion, so that all Singaporeans will have the best chance to fulfil their fullest potential.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We increased the expenditure on national development from $2.4 billion to $3.6 billion, with the bulk of this going into subsidies on public housing, so that every Singaporean household can have a home to call their own.

sections.label: Preschool subsidies and places
sections.summary: Preschool subsidies were enhanced and extended to more families, and Government-supported preschool places will rise from over 50% to 80% by around 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have significantly enhanced preschool subsidies and made them available to more families from this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will also increase the share of Government-supported preschool places from just over 50% today, to 80% by around 2025.

sections.label: Doubling to over $2 billion
sections.summary: Within the next few years, this will double to over $2 billion per year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Within the next few years, this will double to over $2 billion per year.

sections.label: Higher education bursary costs
sections.summary: The cost of bursaries for higher education will rise from $148 million to $198 million per year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The cost of bursaries for higher education will rise from $148 million per year to $198 million per year.

sections.label: Housing grants and income ceilings
sections.summary: First-time flat buyers can get up to $160,000 in housing grants, and income ceilings for subsidised flats and executive condominiums were raised.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the Enhanced Housing Grant, first-time flat buyers can now enjoy up to $160,000 in housing grants.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The monthly household income ceilings for subsidised flats and executive condominiums were raised to $14,000 and $16,000 respectively.

sections.label: Care and Support Package
sections.summary: A $1.6 billion Care and Support Package gives cash payouts to Singaporeans aged 21 and above, and doubles U-Save rebates for eligible HDB households.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To help all Singaporeans with their household expenses during this period of uncertainty, I will provide a comprehensive Care and Support Package for households, amounting to about $1.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: All Singaporeans aged 21 and above in 2020, will receive a one‑off cash payout of $300, $200 or $100, depending on their income.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The annual GST Voucher – U-Save provides rebates to help HDB households with their utilities expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, I will double the amount of U-Save rebates through a one-off GST Voucher – U-Save Special Payment to all eligible HDB households.

sections.label: Workfare Special Payment for lower-income workers
sections.summary: A Workfare Special Payment will be provided to further offset daily living expenses for lower-income workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To further offset daily living expenses for lower-income workers, I will provide a Workfare Special Payment.

sections.label: Basic Retirement Sum amounts by cohort
sections.summary: The BRS is $90,500 for this year's cohort turning 55, $93,000 for 2021 and $96,000 for 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: BRS is currently $90,500 for the cohort turning 55 this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The BRS will be $93,000 for cohorts turning 55 in 2021 and $96,000 for those turning 55 in 2022.

sections.label: Matched Retirement Savings Scheme
sections.summary: A Matched Retirement Savings Scheme from 2021 to 2025 will match cash top-ups to CPF Retirement Accounts up to $600 yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To help those with less CPF savings to save more, I will introduce a Matched Retirement Savings Scheme from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, the Government will match every dollar of cash top‑up made to their CPF Retirement Account, up to an annual cap of $600.

sections.label: Silver Support payouts raised 20%
sections.summary: Silver Support provides cash payouts to the bottom 20% of Singaporeans aged 65 and above, and quarterly payouts will rise by 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Silver Support currently provides cash payouts to the bottom 20% of Singaporeans aged 65 and above, with some support for those slightly above the bottom 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will raise the quarterly cash payouts by 20%.

sections.label: More seniors benefit from Silver Support
sections.summary: About 100,000 more seniors are expected to benefit from the enhanced Silver Support in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Overall, we expect about 100,000 more seniors to benefit from the enhanced Silver Support in 2021.

sections.label: Community Capability Trust funding
sections.summary: MSF and NCSS will set up the Community Capability Trust, with up to $350 million committed together with Tote Board.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The organisation plans to use the Bicentennial Community Fund to develop staff and volunteers and build their inhouse fundraising capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) will set up the Community Capability Trust to fundraise and support our social service sector partners in enhancing their capabilities and capacities to serve the community.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For a start, together with Tote Board, we will provide $200 million to the trust in FY2020 and match up to $150 million in funds raised over the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In total, we will commit up to $350 million for the Community Capability Trust.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit and fund top-ups
sections.summary: The new Enabling Employment Credit replaces SEC and ASEC for PwD employment from 2021 to 2025, and three funds receive top-ups.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In 2018, more than 5,700 employers hiring over 8,600 Singaporean PwDs benefited from SEC.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This Budget, we will introduce the new Enabling Employment Credit (EEC) to provide stronger support for employers of PwDs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The new EEC will replace the current SEC and ASEC schemes for PwD employment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: It will be available for five years, from 2021 to 2025, at a cost of about $31 million per year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This Budget, I will also top up three funds that provide targeted help for the elderly and the lower-income.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will provide top-ups of $750 million to the ElderCare Fund, $500 million to the ComCare Fund and $200 million to MediFund.

sections.label: Urban Solutions and Sustainability research
sections.summary: Close to $1 billion is committed for research in Urban Solutions and Sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will do more to develop new ideas and solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are committing close to $1 billion for research in Urban Solutions and Sustainability.

sections.label: Phasing out ICE vehicles
sections.summary: The vision is to phase out ICE vehicles and have all vehicles run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our vision is to phase out ICE vehicles and have all vehicles run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sections.label: EV Early Adoption Incentive
sections.summary: Buyers of fully electric cars and taxis receive a rebate of up to 45% on the Additional Registration Fee, capped at $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For cars and taxis, I will provide an additional EV Early Adoption Incentive.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Those who purchase fully electric cars and taxis will receive a rebate of up to 45% on the Additional Registration Fee, capped at $20,000.

sections.label: Deploying public car park chargers
sections.summary: By 2030, up to 28,000 chargers are to be deployed at public car parks island-wide.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By 2030, we aim to deploy up to 28,000 chargers at our public car parks island-wide.

sections.label: Lump-sum tax for EVs
sections.summary: A lump-sum tax built into the road tax schedule for EVs is phased in over three years from January 2021, fully implemented by January 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the interim, we will impose a lump-sum tax that will be built into the road tax schedule for EVs to partly account for the loss in fuel excise duties.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This lump-sum tax will be phased in over three years starting from January 2021, with the full quantum implemented by January 2023.

sections.label: Green living and HDB estates
sections.summary: Incentives for energy-efficient appliances, green cover in new housing, community gardens and a new HDB Green Towns Programme are set out.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To encourage households to purchase energy-efficient household appliances, we will introduce incentives to help lower-income households with the cost of these appliances.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: New housing developments will have around 45% to 60% green cover.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, more than 36,000 gardening enthusiasts are nurturing over 1,500 community gardens island-wide.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To make sustainable living a key feature of our HDB estates, we will have a new HDB Green Towns Programme.

sections.label: Coastal and Flood Protection Fund
sections.summary: A new Coastal and Flood Protection Fund will be set up with an initial injection of $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, it is right and prudent that we set aside resources for this.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set up a new Coastal and Flood Protection Fund with an initial injection of $5 billion.

sections.label: Government cyber and data security
sections.summary: $1 billion over three years will build up the Government's cyber and data security capabilities to safeguard citizens' data and critical information infrastructure systems.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As we embark on initiatives to realise our Smart Nation ambitions, we must continue to enhance our cyber capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $1 billion over the next three years to build up the Government's cyber and data security capabilities to safeguard citizens’ data and our critical information infrastructure systems.

sections.label: Surpluses from MAS and stamp duty
sections.summary: This term of Government has more due mainly to exceptional Statutory Board contributions from MAS and increased stamp duty collections, with some surpluses saved and shared.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this term of Government, we happen to have more, mainly due to exceptional Statutory Board contributions from MAS and increased stamp duty collections.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We used some of the unexpected surpluses to save ahead for anticipated needs and shared some of the surpluses with Singaporeans.

sections.label: Fiscal discipline and credit rating
sections.summary: Fiscal discipline has helped Singapore be among a select group of countries with a triple-A credit rating.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our fiscal discipline has helped us to be among a select group of countries with a triple-A credit rating.

sections.label: FY2019 budget deficit figures
sections.summary: For FY2019 an overall budget deficit of $1.7 billion, or 0.3% of GDP, is expected, $1.8 billion lower than forecasted a year ago.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For FY2019, we expect an overall budget deficit of $1.7 billion, or 0.3% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This deficit is $1.8 billion lower than the $3.5 billion deficit forecasted a year ago.

sections.label: Budget position and COVID-19 uncertainty
sections.summary: The Singapore economy faces uncertainty from global risks and COVID-19, so FY2020 Budget will be more expansionary with a $12.3 billion basic deficit.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the coming year, the Singapore economy faces considerable uncertainty, because of heightened risks in the global economy, and the rapidly evolving COVID-19 outbreak.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Hence, for FY2020, our Budget position will be more expansionary, with a larger basic deficit of $12.3 billion.

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund ground-up projects
sections.summary: The Our Singapore Fund, set up in 2016, has committed nearly $4.3 million to over 240 ground-up projects in culture, heritage, arts and sports.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In 2016, we set up the Our Singapore Fund (OSF) to provide funding support for ground-up efforts in the social domain.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since then, OSF has committed nearly $4.3 million to support over 240 ground-up projects in culture, heritage, arts and sports.

sections.label: Partnership funding and SG Eco Fund
sections.summary: $250 million is set aside for partnerships, OSF is topped up and extended beyond 2020, and MEWR will launch an SG Eco Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And we are committed to making partnerships an integral part of how we will build our future Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $250 million to give greater momentum to our partnership efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will top up OSF and extend the Fund beyond 2020 to support more ground-up initiatives that Singaporeans are passionate about, across a wider range of domains.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: MEWR will also be launching an SG Eco Fund to support partnerships with the community and enterprises in our sustainability efforts.

sections.label: National innovation challenges
sections.summary: National innovation challenges have been issued in energy, land and liveability, ageing, urban mobility and AI-enabled healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will help us focus our collective efforts on the challenges that matter and allow us to galvanise good ideas and solutions from the public.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have issued several national innovation challenges to date, in the areas of energy, land and liveability, ageing, urban mobility and AI-enabled healthcare.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Care Support Packages
sections.summary: A $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package and a $1.6 billion Care and Support Package will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In order to reduce the pressure on businesses and our people, I will introduce a $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In order to help Singaporeans meet their daily expenditures, I will also introduce a $1.6 billion Care and Support Package.

sections.label: SkillsFuture, GST and Assurance Package
sections.summary: A SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package is introduced, GST stays at 7% in 2021, and a $6 billion Assurance Package will accompany a GST rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Through SkillsFuture, we encourage lifelong learning, which can bring about lifelong benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will introduce the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package to help locals in their 40s and 50s learn new skills and take on new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Second, we will build a caring and inclusive society together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I have just announced that the GST rate will remain at 7% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: When we raise the GST rate, we will continue to help low-income families and provide more support for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will provide a $6 billion Assurance Package when the GST rate is raised and enhance the existing permanent GST Voucher scheme.

sections.label: Coastal and Flood Protection Fund
sections.summary: The speaker will provide $5 billion to set up a new Coastal and Flood Protection Fund, especially for climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Especially in the area of climate change, I will provide $5 billion to set up a new Coastal and Flood Protection Fund.

sections.label: Budget debate adjournment
sections.summary: The passage states aims to grow the economy, care for Singaporeans, build a sustainable Singapore, and adjourns the debate on the financial policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As one Singapore, we will grow our economy and transform our enterprises, creating opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As one Singapore, we will care for and nurture Singaporeans at every stage of their lives, to build a caring and inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As one Singapore, we will build a liveable and sustainable Singapore in the face of climate change, secure our sovereignty as an independent nation and ensure our fiscal sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Our nation has built up the capital – financial, human, and social – to go the distance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the financial year 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2021." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
